question: In ethylene (C2H4), hybridisation of carbon atoms is:
solution:
The correct answer is__** sp2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hybridisation is the **process of mixing atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals** suitable for the pairing of electrons to form chemical bonds in valence bond theory.
 
• Ethylene is a hydrocarbon with the formula C2H4.
 
• Carbon atoms: Each carbon atom in ethylene forms three sigma bonds (two with hydrogen atoms and one with another carbon atom) and one pi bond (with the other carbon atom).
 
• The carbon atoms in ethylene undergo sp2 hybridisation, which involves the **mixing of one s orbital and two p orbitals** to form three sp2 hybrid orbitals.
 
• The sp2 hybridisation results in a trigonal planar structure with bond angles of approximately 120°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7167c310ffa5e6cbe93ae23b46abb87298745bd97811c62e719b26c7b16ad56.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****sp3 hybridisation:** This involves the mixing of** one s orbital and three p orbitals** to form four sp3 hybrid orbitals, which is seen in methane (CH4).

**sp hybridisation:** This involves the mixing of **one s orbital and one p orbital** to form two sp hybrid orbitals, which is seen in acetylene (C2H2).

**sp3d hybridisation:** This involves the mixing of **one s orbital, three p orbitals, and one d orbital** to form five sp3d hybrid orbitals, which is seen in molecules with trigonal bipyramidal geometry, such as phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5).
